name: Eiche an der Meinhardstrasse

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal ND_101_7, Land Tirol, Naturdenkmaeler Tirol (TIRIS), CC BY 4.0

access: Free: stands on a public street corner in the city centre.
transport: About 250 m straight line from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof (a few minutes on foot).
verify_notes: Wikipedia list (from the Land Tirol survey): Stieleiche, trunk circumference about 2 m at the base, crown rises above the 5th floor of the Landwirtschaftskammer building next door; described as shaping the look of the street. Protected since 1934 (older than most of the list). A Commons photo of Meinhardstrasse dated 2024-01-14 is within lifecheck range (not confirmed to show the tree). Girth is the survey's figure, date of measurement not given. Age not in any source: leave empty. Designated 1934 (register id ND_101_7). Alive: register entry is active (revoked ND rows are listed separately in the Land Tirol data and the de.wikipedia list, which was edited in Sept 2025 to record the felled Blutbuche at the Landestheater, still carries this tree as current). No dated photo or news of this specific trunk seen in this pass; lifecheck's nearby iNaturalist hits were weeds, not the tree, so they prove nothing. Pin is the register point (digitised at 1:1000 to 1:5000), approximate; Wikipedia list gives a coordinate within about 25 m of it. Not checked against OSM (Overpass returns 406 here).

location.neighbourhood: Innsbruck old town, beside the Hofgarten

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal ND_101_24, Land Tirol, Naturdenkmaeler Tirol (TIRIS), CC BY 4.0

access: Free: public street space at the Rennweg, central Innsbruck.
transport: Central Innsbruck; roughly 10 minutes on foot (about 700 m) from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof.
verify_notes: Wikipedia list cites the city's Baumkataster for it: a pyramid-shaped corkscrew fastigiate oak (Quercus robur 'Fastigiata Tortuosa'), probably from North America or East Asia per Wikipedia (the cultivar's origin claim is unsourced there, do not repeat as fact), pointed habit and snaking branches, more than 20 m high, girth more than 3 m (girth_cm 300 is that floor). A cultivar, so an odd specimen rather than an ancient one: the page should sell its shape, not age. Same Rennweg 2 plot held the Blutbuche (felled Sept 2025, see blocked) and a black pine (collapsed Jan 2021, protection revoked 2013). The Hofgarten is next door. name: Alte Foehre am Planoetzenhof
age_estimate: called one of the oldest natural monuments in Tyrol

location.address: Path fork about 100 m above the Planoetzenhof, Hötting

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal ND_101_13, Land Tirol, Naturdenkmaeler Tirol (TIRIS), CC BY 4.0

access: Free: stands at a fork of a public path above the Planoetzenhof, a farm inn on the Hötting hillside. A walk uphill from Hötting.
transport: Hötting hillside, about 2.3 km north-west of Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof by straight line, uphill on foot; check a local bus to Hötting for the approach.
verify_notes: Wikipedia list: 'eines der aeltesten Naturdenkmaeler Tirols' (one of the oldest natural monuments in Tyrol, meaning the protection, designated 1928, not necessarily the tree's age). The trunk originally split about 4 m up into three stems, but the main trunk and the lower branches had to be removed. So a damaged old pine. Species: sources say Foehre/Kiefer only; in Tyrol that is normally Scots pine but no source here says so, hence genus only. No girth, height or age in any source seen. A search for a second description (age, girth) found nothing; Wikipedia Commons has a 2014-05-07 photo of it. This is the most 'old' tree in the set but the one with least data. Designated 1928 (register id ND_101_13). Alive: register entry is active (revoked ND rows are listed separately in the Land Tirol data and the de.wikipedia list, which was edited in Sept 2025 to record the felled Blutbuche at the Landestheater, still carries this tree as current).
